- `ootp-ch26-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Six - Seen and Unforeseen): The High Inquisitor bans possession of The Quibbler across the school and threatens expulsion, extending Ministry information control to school spaces and student property.
- `ootp-ch26-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Six - Seen and Unforeseen): Students evade the Quibbler ban with concealment charms, while teachers forbidden by Decree Twenty-six still show indirect support through ordinary school mechanisms.
- `ootp-ch26-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Six - Seen and Unforeseen): The chapter follows the practical effects of High Inquisitor Quidditch bans into an actual House match, with replacement players, altered team performance, and a student understanding that the ban depends on Umbridge's authority.
- `ootp-ch26-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Six - Seen and Unforeseen): The private Occlumency lessons become reciprocal and risky: a Shield Charm can disrupt Legilimency, expose the teacher's memories, and require use of the Pensieve during instruction.
- `ootp-ch26-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Six - Seen and Unforeseen): Educational Decree Twenty-three lets the High Inquisitor dismiss teachers, but Dumbledore asserts that the headmaster retains authority over whether a dismissed teacher may remain in the castle.
- `ootp-ch26-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Six - Seen and Unforeseen): Dumbledore uses the conditional wording of Educational Decree Twenty-two to appoint Firenze as Divination teacher before the Ministry can fill the post.
- `ootp-ch27-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak): Firenze identifies the Forbidden Forest as his former home, says his herd banished him for working for Dumbledore, and rejects student assumptions that centaurs are human servants.
- `ootp-ch27-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak): Firenze reframes Divination around centaur sky-reading, long observation, Mars as a war omen, burning herbs and leaves, and explicit cautions about interpretive uncertainty.
- `ootp-ch27-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak): Umbridge's case against the D.A. combines a student informant, Floo-policing family connections, prior Hog's Head testimony, Decree Twenty-four timing, and a recovered membership list.
- `ootp-ch27-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak): The headmaster's office crisis confirms active portrait witnesses, Dumbledore's use of Fawkes as an escape route, and a fresh statement that Disapparition is impossible inside Hogwarts.
- `ootp-ch28-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Eight - Snape's Worst Memory): Educational Decree Number Twenty-eight names Umbridge Head of Hogwarts, but the head's office and gargoyle appear to reject her access after Dumbledore's escape.
- `ootp-ch28-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Eight - Snape's Worst Memory): Filch expects Educational Decree Twenty-nine to authorize old-style corporal punishments and notes a Ministry order sought to expel Peeves, while his hidden-route knowledge makes him useful to Umbridge.
- `ootp-ch28-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Eight - Snape's Worst Memory): Umbridge explicitly confirms that school communications and routes are under surveillance, including monitored fireplaces, opened owl post, and Filch watching secret passages.
- `ootp-ch28-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Eight - Snape's Worst Memory): Snape uses Dumbledore's Pensieve to store thoughts before Occlumency, and Harry confirms that a memory can be entered from the artifact in a teacher's office.
- `ootp-ch29-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Nine - Career Advice): The Easter break functions as exam-preparation time for fifth- and seventh-years, combining student-made study schedules, intensive library use, subject review, and continuing Quidditch practice.
- `ootp-ch29-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Nine - Career Advice): Umbridge's control of Hogwarts communications extends to incoming parcels, which can be opened, inspected, rewrapped, and stamped as passed by the High Inquisitor.
- `ootp-ch29-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Nine - Career Advice): Hogwarts implements fifth-year career advice through House-level appointment notices and vocational pamphlets that tie school subjects to institutions such as St. Mungo's, Gringotts, and Ministry departments.
- `ootp-ch29-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Nine - Career Advice): The Auror pathway requires high N.E.W.T. results, character and aptitude tests, strong practical Defense, and subject preparation in Defense, Transfiguration, Charms, and Potions, with teacher-specific N.E.W.T. entry thresholds.
- `ootp-ch29-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Nine - Career Advice): Under Umbridge's surveillance regime, the High Inquisitor's own office fireplace remains the one known unwatched Floo route; Harry reaches it by combining a diversion, Invisibility Cloak, and lock-opening magical knife.
- `ootp-ch29-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Nine - Career Advice): Adult Marauders-era testimony adds that James and Snape's rivalry was mutual, James was admired but arrogant, Lily began dating James in seventh year after he matured, and Lupin did not effectively restrain his friends.
- `ootp-ch29-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Twenty-Nine - Career Advice): The swamp diversion culminates in Umbridge and Filch attempting corporal punishment, Fred and George publicly leaving school, confiscated brooms breaking free, and Peeves accepting a student's parting command.
- `ootp-ch30-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty - Grawp): Fred and George's departure immediately becomes school legend, while the portable swamp persists as a fifth-floor obstruction that staff tacitly allow Umbridge and Filch to manage.
- `ootp-ch30-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty - Grawp): Student resistance broadens into corridor sabotage, prank-product sickouts, attacks on Inquisitorial Squad members, and Peeves-led disruption while most staff decline to help Umbridge.
- `ootp-ch30-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty - Grawp): The final Gryffindor-Ravenclaw match resolves the House Quidditch Cup season, with Gryffindor students carrying Ron into the castle while reclaiming the taunt-song as celebration.
- `ootp-ch30-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty - Grawp): Hagrid uses the Quidditch crowd as cover to lead students secretly from the stands past his cabin and deep into the Forbidden Forest, armed because centaur relations have worsened.
- `ootp-ch30-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty - Grawp): Hagrid expects imminent dismissal under Umbridge's creature-focused suspicion, assumes Grubbly-Plank can cover exam teaching, and frames his remaining secret duty as the reason he has not left.
- `ootp-ch30-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty - Grawp): Hagrid has concealed his sixteen-foot giant half-brother Grawp in the Forbidden Forest, after secretly transporting him from giant country and trying to teach him English and manners.
- `ootp-ch30-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty - Grawp): The centaur herd asserts territorial authority and separate law inside the Forest, condemns Firenze's teaching as betrayal, spares schoolchildren as innocents, and warns Hagrid about Grawp.
- `ootp-ch31-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-One - O.W.L.s): Final O.W.L. preparation changes normal teaching into review sessions, intensifies peer anxiety, and produces illicit exam-aid trading among examination-year students.
- `ootp-ch31-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-One - O.W.L.s): McGonagall gives the official O.W.L. procedure, including two-week scheduling, morning theory papers, afternoon practicals, a night Astronomy practical, banned cheating aids, and July owl-post results.
- `ootp-ch31-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-One - O.W.L.s): O.W.L. written papers transform the Great Hall into an individual-desk examination hall, while practicals are conducted by examiners testing named spells and, in Harry's case, awarding a bonus Patronus opportunity.
- `ootp-ch31-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-One - O.W.L.s): The Care of Magical Creatures O.W.L. practical tests creature identification, safe handling, feeding and cleaning, and treatment knowledge on the lawn by the Forbidden Forest.
- `ootp-ch31-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-One - O.W.L.s): A formal Astronomy O.W.L. practical is interrupted by an armed Ministry-backed staff seizure attempt, exposing students to Umbridge's nighttime removal tactics, Hagrid's resistance, and McGonagall's injury.
- `ootp-ch31-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-One - O.W.L.s): The History of Magic O.W.L. confirms advanced Hogwarts historical curriculum topics: goblin riots and wand law, a 1749 Statute of Secrecy breach, and the formation politics of the International Confederation of Wizards.
- `ootp-ch32-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Two - Out of the Fire): The aftermath of the History of Magic O.W.L. shows an examiner's practical response to student collapse and confirms McGonagall's removal from Hogwarts to St. Mungo's after multiple Stunning Spells.
- `ootp-ch32-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Two - Out of the Fire): With the usual adult channels absent, students treat Umbridge's office fire as the remaining practical way to check Order headquarters from inside Hogwarts.
- `ootp-ch32-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Two - Out of the Fire): The students combine corridor misdirection, concealment, and a magical lock-opening knife to enter the High Inquisitor's office after earlier niffler attacks exposed a window weakness.
- `ootp-ch32-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Two - Out of the Fire): The office fireplace successfully connects Hogwarts to Grimmauld Place by Floo, allowing a head-only communication link while the user's body remains in the office.
- `ootp-ch32-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Two - Out of the Fire): Umbridge responds to prior office intrusions by adding Stealth Sensoring Spells to the doorway, enabling her to catch a concealed entry and immediately confiscate student wands.
- `ootp-ch32-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Two - Out of the Fire): The Inquisitorial Squad operates as a physical enforcement arm for Umbridge, capturing, gagging, and restraining students while using Filch's information to defeat a diversion.
- `ootp-ch32-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Two - Out of the Fire): Umbridge attempts to escalate a school interrogation from Veritaserum to the illegal Cruciatus Curse and privately admits she ordered the previous summer's Dementor attack on Harry.
- `ootp-ch33-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Three - Fight and Flight): The scene traces a crisis route from Umbridge's office through the entrance hall and front doors into the grounds while ordinary school dining continues nearby.
- `ootp-ch33-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Three - Fight and Flight): Hermione exploits known Forest dangers by deliberately attracting centaur attention, resulting in an armed centaur encirclement deep inside the Forest.
- `ootp-ch33-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Three - Fight and Flight): The centaurs answer Umbridge's spell and insults by physically removing the acting headmistress and destroying her wand, while sparing Harry and Hermione only provisionally as young.
- `ootp-ch33-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Three - Fight and Flight): The herd frames human intrusion as arrogance, rejects any role as human servants, condemns Firenze as a traitor, and denies wizard laws and superiority.
- `ootp-ch33-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Three - Fight and Flight): Grawp's concealed presence escalates into open conflict with the centaurs, showing that Hagrid's hidden giant has crossed from private secret to territorial crisis.
- `ootp-ch33-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Three - Fight and Flight): The school thestrals become emergency long-distance transport: visible only to death-witnesses, attracted by blood like raw meat, and trusted to locate a rider's intended destination.
- `ootp-ch34-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries): The chapter confirms that Hogwarts thestrals can carry multiple student riders on an unscheduled long-distance flight from the school grounds to London, even when some riders cannot see their mounts.
- `ootp-ch34-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries): The Ministry visitor entrance remains automated after hours, issuing badges and search/wand-registration instructions, but the manual Atrium security post is deserted during the crisis.
- `ootp-ch35-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Five - Beyond the Veil): The Department's prophecy records appear to have an access restriction: only the subject of a prophecy can retrieve it, forcing Voldemort to manipulate Harry rather than collect the orb directly.
- `ootp-ch35-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Five - Beyond the Veil): When Department prophecy orbs break, they release smoky or ghostlike figures that speak fragments of the recorded prophecies before dissolving.
- `ootp-ch35-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Five - Beyond the Veil): The Time Room contains dangerous temporal artifacts: a cabinet repeatedly repairs and breaks, and the bell jar can cycle a person's body part between adult and infant states.
- `ootp-ch35-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Five - Beyond the Veil): Department brain specimens are active and dangerous: a summoned brain releases ribbon-like thought tentacles that bind Ron and resist Harry's cutting spell.
- `ootp-ch35-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Five - Beyond the Veil): The veiled arch is lethally consequential: Sirius falls through it, fails to reappear, and Lupin treats the passage beyond the veil as irreversible.
- `ootp-ch36-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Only One He Ever Feared): The Department's rotating antechamber can expose the correct exit route in response to a direct request, leading from the research rooms back to the lift corridor and Atrium.
- `ootp-ch36-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Only One He Ever Feared): Dumbledore turns the Ministry's Fountain of Magical Brethren into active combat and communication assets: statues shield Harry, pin Bellatrix, engage Voldemort, and bring Fudge from the fireplaces.
- `ootp-ch36-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Only One He Ever Feared): Fawkes protects Dumbledore by swallowing a Killing Curse and immediately rebirths from flame, while Dumbledore counters Voldemort's snake and water-based attacks.
- `ootp-ch36-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Only One He Ever Feared): Voldemort can invade Harry's body or mind through their scar connection, but Harry's emotional attachment to Sirius disrupts the possession.
- `ootp-ch36-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Only One He Ever Feared): The Ministry finally witnesses Voldemort's return; Dumbledore has escaped Death Eaters contained in the Death Chamber, creates a disputed Portkey to send Harry back to Hogwarts, and compels Fudge to remove Umbridge and stop the search for Hagrid.
- `ootp-ch37-001` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Lost Prophecy): Dumbledore's office is described as restored after Umbridge's occupation, barred to everyone except the rightful headmaster, able to confine Harry, and monitored by active former-head portraits.
- `ootp-ch37-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Lost Prophecy): Dumbledore identifies Harry's scar as a connection forged with Voldemort, says it allowed emotional and mental contact, and explains that Occlumency was meant to defend against manipulation, spying, and possession.
- `ootp-ch37-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Lost Prophecy): Dumbledore confirms that Ministry-held prophecies are heavily protected and that anyone other than a named subject who tries to remove one risks madness.
- `ootp-ch37-005` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Lost Prophecy): Dumbledore says Lily's sacrifice left blood-based protection in Harry and Petunia, that Petunia sealed his charm by taking Harry in, and that returning to that home once a year keeps Voldemort from harming him there.
- `ootp-ch37-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Lost Prophecy): Dumbledore heard the first prophecy while interviewing Sybill Trelawney for the Divination post at the Hog's Head and later retrieves the memory into the Pensieve to replay the prophecy exactly.
- `ootp-ch37-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Lost Prophecy): Dumbledore explains that the prophecy initially could have meant either Harry or Neville, but Voldemort's attack marked Harry, caused the Hall record to be relabeled, and turned incomplete overheard information into the decisive cause of the conflict.
- `ootp-ch38-002` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Eight - The Second War Begins): After Dumbledore's return, Flitwick removes most of the portable swamp but preserves a small roped-off patch as admired magic, while Umbridge is later chased from Hogwarts by Peeves with only halfhearted restraint from staff.
- `ootp-ch38-003` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Eight - The Second War Begins): After Trelawney's return and Firenze's banishment from the centaur herd, Hogwarts appears to retain both as Divination teachers.
- `ootp-ch38-004` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Eight - The Second War Begins): McGonagall awards fifty points each to Harry, the Weasleys, Longbottom, Granger, and Lovegood for alerting the world to Voldemort's return, causing rubies and sapphires to fall in the House hourglasses before Snape's deduction removes a few rubies.
- `ootp-ch38-006` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Eight - The Second War Begins): Nearly Headless Nick says only wizards can return as ghosts, very few choose that path, ghosts are an imprint rather than true life, and deeper secrets of death are studied by learned wizards in the Department of Mysteries.
- `ootp-ch38-007` (Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, Chapter Thirty-Eight - The Second War Begins): D.A. members use the practical hexes and jinxes Harry taught them to stop an attempted train ambush, showing student-led Defense training producing usable collective defensive skill outside the classroom.
- `poa-ch01-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter One - Owl Post): The chapter names Bathilda Bagshot's A History of Magic as a Hogwarts homework source and gives a short excerpted historical claim about medieval witch burning and Flame-Freezing Charms.
- `poa-ch01-002` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter One - Owl Post): The chapter confirms that Hogwarts teachers assign holiday work and that students may need school books and writing materials during summer, even when guardians restrict access.
- `poa-ch01-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter One - Owl Post): The chapter shows owl post delivering personal mail and an official Hogwarts-crest letter to a student during summer vacation.
- `poa-ch01-004` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter One - Owl Post): The chapter confirms Percy's appointment as Head Boy through a letter, badge, and two student correspondents.
- `poa-ch01-005` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter One - Owl Post): The chapter gives a returning-student Hogwarts letter with travel logistics, booklist enclosure, and the third-year Hogsmeade permission-form requirement.
- `poa-ch01-006` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter One - Owl Post): The chapter introduces a named, physically aggressive magical book sent by Hagrid as something useful for the coming school year.
- `poa-ch01-007` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter One - Owl Post): The chapter adds broom maintenance materials and restates Harry's unusual place on a Hogwarts House Quidditch team, with his Nimbus Two Thousand as prized equipment.
- `poa-ch02-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Two - Aunt Marge's Big Mistake): The chapter corroborates Hogsmeade visits as a third-year privilege requiring a signed permission form and shows the practical dependence on a guardian's signature.
- `poa-ch02-002` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Two - Aunt Marge's Big Mistake): The chapter shows Harry concealing school-related materials and interrupting owl contact during a Muggle-relative visit, while still preserving student-to-student communication by note.
- `poa-ch02-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Two - Aunt Marge's Big Mistake): The chapter reiterates the underage outside-school magic restriction and links repeat detected magic at Harry's residence with possible expulsion from Hogwarts.
- `poa-ch02-004` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Two - Aunt Marge's Big Mistake): The chapter gives another glimpse of the broomcare handbook as a practical in-universe source with named charm and maintenance guidance.
- `poa-ch03-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Three - The Knight Bus): The chapter shows Ministry response to accidental underage magic, including reversal and memory modification, and then shows Fudge treating punishment and Hogwarts expulsion as discretionary under changed circumstances.
- `poa-ch03-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Three - The Knight Bus): The chapter corroborates the Leaky Cauldron as the access point to Diagon Alley and adds a supervised temporary lodging arrangement for a Hogwarts student in the pre-term supply district.
- `poa-ch03-004` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Three - The Knight Bus): The chapter confirms that Harry customarily stays at Hogwarts during Christmas and Easter breaks and shows an extraordinary alternative lodging plan for the remaining summer vacation.
- `poa-ch03-005` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Three - The Knight Bus): The chapter confirms that even the Minister of Magic will not substitute for a parent or guardian signature on the third-year Hogsmeade permission form.
- `poa-ch04-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Four - The Leaky Cauldron): The chapter corroborates the Leaky Cauldron courtyard entrance into Diagon Alley and shows a student temporarily living near the supply district under an instruction not to re-enter Muggle London.
- `poa-ch04-002` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Four - The Leaky Cauldron): The chapter shows holiday essays continuing during the pre-term period and names Florean Fortescue as a knowledgeable helper on medieval witch-burning history.
- `poa-ch04-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Four - The Leaky Cauldron): The chapter provides direct booklist confirmation for third-year supplies, including subject-specific texts and recurring equipment purchases such as robes and potion ingredients.
- `poa-ch04-004` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Four - The Leaky Cauldron): The chapter confirms a set of third-year elective subjects in active use and clarifies the framing of Muggle Studies as wizarding analysis of Muggles.
- `poa-ch04-005` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Four - The Leaky Cauldron): The chapter shows students buying or bringing pets before term and assumes that cats and rats can sleep in House dormitories, while owls serve personal or family mail roles.
- `poa-ch04-006` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Four - The Leaky Cauldron): The chapter confirms visible Head Boy insignia, family recognition of the office, and the distinction between Head Boy and prefect appointments.
- `poa-ch05-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Five - The Dementor): The chapter corroborates the hidden King's Cross barrier route, the platform crowd of magical families, and the start-of-term loading of trunks and student pets onto the Hogwarts Express.
- `poa-ch05-002` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Five - The Dementor): Hermione treats Hogsmeade as a historically interesting settlement from a named source, while the same scene reinforces Hogsmeade weekend access as dependent on a signed permission form.
- `poa-ch05-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Five - The Dementor): The chapter adds observed evidence for an incoming teacher traveling on the Hogwarts Express and confirms student awareness of repeated Defense Against the Dark Arts turnover.
- `poa-ch05-005` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Five - The Dementor): The chapter corroborates the split arrival procedure at Hogsmeade station, with first-years directed to the lake while older students ride stagecoaches through the gates to the castle.
- `poa-ch05-006` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Five - The Dementor): The chapter provides the official student-facing rule for the dementor security period, including boundary placement, movement restrictions, and senior-student monitoring responsibilities.
- `poa-ch05-007` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Five - The Dementor): The start-of-term feast formally records two staff changes, including Hagrid replacing Kettleburn in Care of Magical Creatures while retaining gamekeeping duties.
- `poa-ch06-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Six - Talons and Tea Leaves): The chapter confirms active third-year elective scheduling and shows Hermione's exceptional overloaded timetable being handled through McGonagall.
- `poa-ch06-002` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Six - Talons and Tea Leaves): The chapter adds a concrete North Tower route, a named portrait figure who moves through frames to guide students, and a magical trapdoor-ladder entrance to the Divination classroom.
- `poa-ch06-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Six - Talons and Tea Leaves): The chapter supplies the first live Divination syllabus evidence and connects the lesson to a named course text, Unfogging the Future.
- `poa-ch06-004` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Six - Talons and Tea Leaves): The chapter frames Animagi as Transfiguration subject matter and gives McGonagall's faculty perspective that Divination is an imprecise branch of magic, distinct from the rare status of true seers.
- `poa-ch06-005` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Six - Talons and Tea Leaves): The chapter confirms the physical location and cross-House pairing of the first third-year Care of Magical Creatures lesson and gives the handling method for the assigned biting textbook.
- `poa-ch06-006` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Six - Talons and Tea Leaves): The chapter gives detailed practical creature-handling instruction for hippogriffs and shows Hogwarts students learning through supervised contact with dangerous live creatures.
- `poa-ch06-007` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Six - Talons and Tea Leaves): The chapter shows a classroom injury triggering hospital-wing treatment, governor attention, and concern about whether a teacher's lesson plan was too advanced for students.
- `poa-ch07-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Seven - The Boggart in the Wardrobe): The chapter gives another practical Potions class with cross-House grouping, named ingredients, a potion outcome test on a toad, and House-point discipline.
- `poa-ch07-002` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Seven - The Boggart in the Wardrobe): The chapter confirms that Malfoy's family escalates the Care of Magical Creatures injury to both governors and the Ministry in an attempt to threaten Hagrid's position.
- `poa-ch07-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Seven - The Boggart in the Wardrobe): The chapter strengthens the exceptional-course-load thread by showing Hermione carrying many books and behaving as if she is managing overlapping academic demands.
- `poa-ch07-004` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Seven - The Boggart in the Wardrobe): Lupin's first Defense Against the Dark Arts class is explicitly practical rather than book-based and uses a different castle room for the exercise.
- `poa-ch07-005` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Seven - The Boggart in the Wardrobe): The chapter adds another example of Peeves disrupting school infrastructure and shows a teacher using a spell demonstration to manage him in front of students.
- `poa-ch08-001` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Eight - Flight of the Fat Lady): The chapter gives a short third-year Defense Against the Dark Arts sequence under Lupin, moving from boggarts to Red Caps, kappas, and an upcoming grindylow lesson.
- `poa-ch08-002` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Eight - Flight of the Fat Lady): The chapter corroborates Hogwarts House Quidditch structure with a captain-led seasonal meeting, team positions, Cup stakes, locker-room setting, and regular practice schedule.
- `poa-ch08-003` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Eight - Flight of the Fat Lady): The chapter shows the school-side enforcement of Hogsmeade permission forms through Head-of-House collection, strict guardian-signature interpretation, and caretaker name checks.
- `poa-ch08-004` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Eight - Flight of the Fat Lady): The chapter provides another observed instance of Gryffindor Tower's password-controlled Fat Lady portrait entrance and shows the portrait behaving as an interactive resident gatekeeper.
- `poa-ch08-006` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Eight - Flight of the Fat Lady): The chapter corroborates the Halloween feast as a decorated Great Hall tradition and adds ghostly entertainment, including formation gliding and Nick's beheading reenactment.
- `poa-ch08-007` (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Chapter Eight - Flight of the Fat Lady): The chapter records a breach of Gryffindor Tower's portrait entrance, showing portrait mobility, Head Boy escalation, headmaster response, Filch's search role, and Peeves as an informant.

- `ps-ch14-001` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fourteen - Norbert the Norwegian Ridgeback): The chapter shows exam preparation intensifying before the end of first year, with teacher-assigned homework, student study schedules, library work, and named study material.
- `ps-ch14-003` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fourteen - Norbert the Norwegian Ridgeback): Hagrid gives the clearest evidence so far that the Stone is protected by multiple staff members, including Fluffy and teacher-made enchantments, while still keeping the details secret from students.
- `ps-ch14-006` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fourteen - Norbert the Norwegian Ridgeback): The chapter provides a concrete nighttime route through the entrance hall, staircases, corridors, and the tallest tower, with Peeves and Filch as navigation or enforcement obstacles.
- `ps-ch14-007` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fourteen - Norbert the Norwegian Ridgeback): The chapter shows a teacher applying detention and House-point discipline for nighttime wandering, with later corridor enforcement by Filch.
- `ps-ch15-001` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fifteen - The Forbidden Forest): The chapter identifies the tallest Astronomy Tower as out of bounds except for classes and shows Filch escalating the nighttime violation to Professor McGonagall.
- `ps-ch15-002` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fifteen - The Forbidden Forest): The chapter gives a large-scale House-point deduction for nighttime rule-breaking and confirms that giant hourglasses visibly record House points.
- `ps-ch15-003` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fifteen - The Forbidden Forest): The chapter again presents the Hogwarts library as a large research setting and reinforces student secrecy around the Stone and Fluffy.
- `ps-ch15-004` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fifteen - The Forbidden Forest): The chapter shows detention logistics: written notices, a late-night meeting point, caretaker escort, Hagrid's role in supervising the punishment, and Filch's comments about older disciplinary methods.
- `ps-ch15-005` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Fifteen - The Forbidden Forest): The chapter gives concrete Forbidden Forest geography and a supervised search protocol using paths, student groups, Fang, and colored wand sparks.
- `ps-ch16-001` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Sixteen - Through the Trapdoor): The chapter gives concrete end-of-year assessment details, including anti-cheating quills, written papers, practical exams, subject-specific tasks, and History of Magic topics.
- `ps-ch16-003` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Sixteen - Through the Trapdoor): Hagrid reveals that the method for bypassing Fluffy is music and that this secret was extracted from him during the dragon-egg encounter.
- `ps-ch16-004` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Sixteen - Through the Trapdoor): The chapter combines staff confidence in the Stone protections with disciplinary warnings around renewed nighttime wandering and access to the third-floor corridor.
- `ps-ch16-005` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Sixteen - Through the Trapdoor): The chapter reveals the first layers below the trapdoor: music calms Fluffy, the trapdoor leads into a deep chamber, and Devil's Snare functions as a plant-based protection requiring Herbology knowledge.
- `ps-ch16-006` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Sixteen - Through the Trapdoor): The chapter reveals a flying-key chamber that depends on broom skill and a transfigured chess challenge later attributed to Flitwick and McGonagall respectively.
- `ps-ch16-007` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Sixteen - Through the Trapdoor): The chapter reveals a troll room followed by Snape's potion-and-fire puzzle, where logic rather than spell-casting determines safe passage forward or back.
- `ps-ch17-001` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Seventeen - The Man with Two Faces): Quirrell confirms that the earlier broom incident was his attack, not Snape's, and says Snape tried to protect Harry through counter-magic and later refereeing.
- `ps-ch17-002` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Seventeen - The Man with Two Faces): Quirrell reveals that the Halloween troll incident was deliberate, that Snape used the diversion to intercept him at the third floor, and that Dumbledore's Mirror protection blocks Quirrell from finding the Stone.
- `ps-ch17-003` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Seventeen - The Man with Two Faces): Dumbledore explains the final Mirror-based protection for the Stone and the desire-based condition for retrieving it.
- `ps-ch17-005` (Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Chapter Seventeen - The Man with Two Faces): The chapter documents the end-of-year feast as the setting for House Cup standings, headmaster-awarded last-minute points, and immediate Great Hall decoration changes for the winning House.

## Later Editorial Notes

- `cos-ch01-003` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter One - The Worst Birthday): The chapter shows owl post as Harry's expected channel for holiday contact with friends, Hogwarts, and the wider wizarding world, and shows how guardian interference can cut off that contact.
- `cos-ch02-001` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Two - Dobby's Warning): Dobby describes house-elves as bound servants of wizarding families who require release by the family to become free.
- `cos-ch02-002` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Two - Dobby's Warning): Dobby claims he has known for months about a plot targeting Hogwarts during Harry's second year and tries to prevent Harry from returning.
- `cos-ch02-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Two - Dobby's Warning): The chapter confirms that Harry's apparent holiday isolation was caused by Dobby intercepting letters from school friends and Hagrid.
- `cos-ch03-002` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Three - The Burrow): The chapter adds peer-supplied house-elf lore about magic-use permission and social association with wealthy old wizarding households.
- `cos-ch03-003` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Three - The Burrow): The passage confirms ordinary student holiday correspondence by owl, distinguishes family owls by name and ownership, and links Percy's prefect status to separate owl use and correspondence.
- `cos-ch03-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Three - The Burrow): The chapter gives legal and Ministry context for enchanted Muggle artifacts, including enforcement raids, Memory Charms after Muggle exposure, Muggle-baiting, and Arthur's loophole around the flying car.
- `cos-ch04-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Four - At Flourish and Blotts): The exchange confirms Muggle-born academic success at Hogwarts through Hermione's exam performance and shows blood-status prejudice responding to merit-based school achievement.
- `cos-ch07-006` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Seven - Mudbloods and Murmurs): The chapter records differentiated detention assignments, trophy-room cleaning without magic, Filch's custodial role, Lockhart's office detention, and the first observed hidden voice connected to the Chamber of Secrets crisis.
- `cos-ch08-006` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eight - The Deathday Party): The chapter gives the first visible Chamber of Secrets attack marker: a threatening wall message, Mrs. Norris petrified beneath it, and a route from the dungeon passage to a second-floor corridor after the Halloween feast.
- `cos-ch10-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Ten - The Rogue Bludger): The match shows a magical-sport safety incident and gives a concrete storage detail for Hogwarts Quidditch equipment between practices and matches.
- `cos-ch10-006` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Ten - The Rogue Bludger): The chapter moves the Chamber evidence from warning and legend into staff-recognized crisis evidence: Dobby confirms a prior opening, Colin is petrified, and Dumbledore says the Chamber is open again.
- `cos-ch11-003` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eleven - The Dueling Club): The chapter documents an authorized extracurricular defensive-practice session using the Great Hall, staff demonstration, combative wand stance, and the Disarming Charm.
- `cos-ch11-006` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eleven - The Dueling Club): The chapter records another Chamber-related attack affecting both a student and a ghost, plus the immediate staff response and the different handling needed for a petrified ghost.
- `cos-ch12-002` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Twelve - The Polyjuice Potion): The chapter shows the Christmas-holiday residence system under emergency pressure, with students leaving by train, a smaller group staying in the castle, and a prefect framing his presence as teacher support.
- `cos-ch12-006` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Twelve - The Polyjuice Potion): The chapter identifies Lucius Malfoy as a Hogwarts governor and shows external political pressure around the school, the headmaster, and the public handling of the Chamber attacks.
- `cos-ch13-003` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Thirteen - The Very Secret Diary): The chapter records a staff-arranged Valentine's Day morale event during the Chamber crisis, including Great Hall decoration, schoolwide message delivery, and teacher-annoying class disruption.
- `cos-ch13-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Thirteen - The Very Secret Diary): The diary presents itself as a magical memory-bearing source for covered-up events at Hogwarts and can draw a reader into an embedded memory scene.
- `cos-ch14-001` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fourteen - Cornelius Fudge): The chapter links Mandrake maturation in Herbology to the planned medical revival of petrified students in the hospital wing.
- `cos-ch14-003` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fourteen - Cornelius Fudge): The chapter shows a schoolwide emergency overriding Quidditch and routing students back through House structures for further instructions.
- `cos-ch14-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fourteen - Cornelius Fudge): The chapter records a severe Chamber-crisis lockdown after the double petrification, including teacher escorts, activity cancellations, bathroom accompaniment, and closure warnings.
- `cos-ch14-005` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fourteen - Cornelius Fudge): The chapter shows Ministry intervention during a Hogwarts safety crisis, including a precautionary removal tied to prior school discipline and pressure from governors.
- `cos-ch14-006` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fourteen - Cornelius Fudge): The chapter confirms that Hogwarts has twelve governors and that they can suspend a headmaster through a signed order.
- `cos-ch14-007` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fourteen - Cornelius Fudge): The chapter gives Dumbledore's statement about stepping aside under governor authority while preserving a loyalty-based idea of continued headmaster influence and help at Hogwarts.
- `cos-ch15-001` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fifteen - Aragog): The chapter shows hospital wing visitor restrictions tightening during the Chamber crisis, with Madam Pomfrey treating the ward as a possible target for a returning attacker.
- `cos-ch15-002` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Fifteen - Aragog): The chapter continues the Chamber-crisis lockdown by showing teacher-supervised movement and evening common-room confinement.
- `cos-ch16-001` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Sixteen - The Chamber of Secrets): The chapter shows ordinary assessment continuing during the Chamber crisis because school leadership is trying to keep Hogwarts running normally while it remains open.
- `cos-ch16-002` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Sixteen - The Chamber of Secrets): The chapter confirms the Mandrake remedy has reached usable maturity and connects Herbology-grown plants directly to hospital-wing recovery and crisis investigation.
- `cos-ch16-003` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Sixteen - The Chamber of Secrets): The chapter gives an in-universe library source for basilisk lore and shows Hermione using that source to infer the monster's identity and route through Hogwarts plumbing.
- `cos-ch16-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Sixteen - The Chamber of Secrets): The chapter shows staff labor under the Chamber lockdown, including class escorts, night guard duty, and corridor patrols.
- `cos-ch16-005` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Sixteen - The Chamber of Secrets): The chapter records the most severe Chamber-crisis escalation: a student taken into the Chamber, school closure, House-based notification, and emergency departure by Hogwarts Express.
- `cos-ch17-002` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Seventeen - The Heir of Slytherin): Riddle's diary is confirmed as a magical memory source that could possess and direct a student, making it the mechanism behind the current Chamber opening.
- `cos-ch17-005` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Seventeen - The Heir of Slytherin): The chapter shows Dumbledore's phoenix delivering the school Sorting Hat, which then produces a sword in direct response to Harry's need.
- `cos-ch18-002` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eighteen - Dobby's Reward): The chapter combines headmaster disciplinary discretion for Ginny with hospital-wing recovery after the Chamber crisis, including Mandrake juice for petrified victims.
- `cos-ch18-003` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eighteen - Dobby's Reward): The headmaster turns a major rule-breaking rescue into formal school honors, a feast, and large House-point awards.
- `cos-ch18-004` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eighteen - Dobby's Reward): The chapter identifies the sword pulled from the Sorting Hat as Godric Gryffindor's and links its appearance to true Gryffindor identity.
- `cos-ch18-005` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eighteen - Dobby's Reward): The chapter shows the governors reversing Dumbledore's suspension under crisis pressure and records Lucius Malfoy's later removal from the board.
- `cos-ch18-006` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eighteen - Dobby's Reward): The chapter ties the diary's route into Hogwarts supplies to Lucius Malfoy and demonstrates house-elf manumission through clothing.
- `cos-ch18-007` (Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Chapter Eighteen - Dobby's Reward): The chapter records end-of-year operations after the Chamber crisis, including an extraordinary feast, House Cup result, canceled exams and classes, and the train journey home.
- `dh-ch01-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter One - The Dark Lord Ascending): The Death Eater council treats Harry's protective removal as a planned Order operation and contrasts Snape's source with Dawlish's false Auror leak.
- `dh-ch01-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter One - The Dark Lord Ascending): The safe house is described as protected by both Order and Ministry enchantments, but its security depends on whether a fallen Ministry can help reveal and undo them.
- `dh-ch01-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter One - The Dark Lord Ascending): Death Eater agents inside the Department of Magical Transport can monitor Apparition and Floo use, making Ministry-regulated transport unsafe for the Order.
- `dh-ch01-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter One - The Dark Lord Ascending): Voldemort frames old family trees, Muggle-born connections, and werewolf marriage as contamination to be pruned from both family and society.
- `dh-ch01-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter One - The Dark Lord Ascending): Charity Burbage is identified as the recent Hogwarts Muggle Studies professor; Voldemort condemns both her class framing of Muggles and her Daily Prophet defense of Muggle-borns.
- `dh-ch02-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Two - In Memoriam): The Daily Prophet presents Skeeter's biography as a contested in-universe source on Dumbledore, explicitly setting Doge's obituary against revisionist claims about his youth and public career.
- `dh-ch03-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Three - The Dursleys Departing): Harry states that the protective charm tied to his underage status will break when he turns seventeen, exposing both Harry and the Dursleys to Voldemort's targeting.
- `dh-ch03-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Three - The Dursleys Departing): The Order treats the Ministry as unreliable for Dursley protection because of suspected infiltration, while Kingsley is already assigned to protect the Muggle Prime Minister.
- `dh-ch03-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Three - The Dursleys Departing): Harry describes wartime Muggle-visible disasters as Voldemort-driven attacks and identifies dementor-created fogs, Death Eaters, and possible Inferi as threats to exposed Muggles.
- `dh-ch03-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Three - The Dursleys Departing): Dedalus plans to avoid magic in Harry's underage household, drive the Dursleys away first, then Disapparate them to a safe location timed with Harry's own departure and the charm's failure.
- `dh-ch04-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Four - The Seven Potters): Moody says Pius Thicknesse has criminalized connecting Privet Drive to the Floo Network, placing a Portkey there, or Apparating in or out, while Harry's Trace would reveal any spell cast to remove him.
- `dh-ch04-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Four - The Seven Potters): Moody states that Lily's protection ends when Harry comes of age or stops calling Privet Drive home; the Order therefore uses false scheduling, twelve protected connected houses, and a Portkey from Tonks's parents' house to the Burrow.
- `dh-ch04-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Four - The Seven Potters): The Order creates six Polyjuice decoys of Harry, each paired with a protector, because Death Eaters are expected to try to capture Harry while killing escorts.
- `dh-ch04-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Four - The Seven Potters): The Order assigns paired decoy routes using brooms, thestrals, and Sirius Black's flying motorbike, with simultaneous departure preserving the diversion and Arthur Weasley's emergency modifications on the bike.
- `dh-ch04-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Four - The Seven Potters): The ambush shows Death Eaters waiting in force over a Muggle area, Order transport under lethal attack, Arthur's modified motorbike deploying emergency defenses, and Harry's signature Disarming Charm revealing the real target.
- `dh-ch04-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Four - The Seven Potters): The chase records Voldemort's unsupported flight, a rare independent reaction from Harry's wand producing golden fire, Voldemort's demand for another wand, and the crash landing at the protected destination.
- `dh-ch05-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Five - Fallen Warrior): Ted Tonks states that the safe-house protective charms should keep attackers at least a hundred yards away, and Harry connects Voldemort's disappearance to crossing that barrier.
- `dh-ch05-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Five - Fallen Warrior): The evacuation relay uses timed ordinary-object Portkeys from protected houses to the Burrow, with staggered return objects and expected arrival order for each pair.
- `dh-ch05-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Five - Fallen Warrior): After the ambush, Order members verify identities with private questions, and Lupin notes that Polyjuice Potion is designed only for human use, making Hagrid a different kind of risk case.
- `dh-ch05-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Five - Fallen Warrior): Lupin identifies Harry's repeated use of Expelliarmus under lethal threat as a recognizable combat pattern, while Harry defends not stunning an Imperiused man hundreds of feet in the air.
- `dh-ch05-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Five - Fallen Warrior): Kingsley infers a hushed-up Azkaban breakout from Stan and Travers, while George's cursed-off ear confirms Sectumsempra's permanent injury risk and Dark Magic healing limits.
- `dh-ch05-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Five - Fallen Warrior): Bill reports that Voldemort killed Moody after Mundungus Disapparated, and the Order debrief concludes that the enemy knew the date but not the full seven-Harry decoy plan.
- `dh-ch05-007` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Five - Fallen Warrior): Harry reports that his wand independently produced unknown golden fire, and a scar vision shows Voldemort torturing Ollivander because Lucius Malfoy's wand failed against Harry's wand connection.
- `dh-ch06-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Six - The Ghoul in Pajamas): Ron says Harry cannot begin the Horcrux hunt until the Trace breaks at seventeen, while Molly confirms that Harry, Ron, and Hermione intend to abandon their Hogwarts education for Dumbledore's mission.
- `dh-ch06-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Six - The Ghoul in Pajamas): After Dumbledore's death, everyone to whom he revealed Grimmauld Place becomes a Secret-Keeper, weakening the Fidelius protection enough that the Burrow replaces it as Order headquarters; Moody also left curses meant to keep Snape out and bind his tongue.
- `dh-ch06-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Six - The Ghoul in Pajamas): Bill says the Daily Prophet has not reported Moody's death, Arthur thinks the Ministry is avoiding Harry's underage-magic hearing to suppress Voldemort's attack, and he doubts the public story that Hogwarts's Muggle Studies professor resigned.
- `dh-ch06-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Six - The Ghoul in Pajamas): Hermione chooses to bring Hogwarts: A History on the Horcrux hunt, saying that even if they are not returning to Hogwarts she would not feel right without it.
- `dh-ch06-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Six - The Ghoul in Pajamas): Hermione has modified her parents' memories and sent them to Australia, while Ron's family will use a transformed ghoul with spattergroit as a cover story for his failure to return to Hogwarts.
- `dh-ch07-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Seven - The Will of Albus Dumbledore): Harry's seventeenth birthday immediately ends the practical Trace constraint on his own spellcasting, and Mrs. Weasley identifies a watch as the traditional gift when a wizard comes of age.
- `dh-ch07-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Seven - The Will of Albus Dumbledore): The Ministry relies on the Decree for Justifiable Confiscation to inspect Dumbledore's will contents for thirty-one days, supposedly requiring evidence that bequeathed objects are illegal or dangerous.
- `dh-ch07-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Seven - The Will of Albus Dumbledore): Scrimgeour says Dumbledore made few personal bequests and left most possessions, including his private library, magical instruments, and other effects, to Hogwarts.
- `dh-ch07-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Seven - The Will of Albus Dumbledore): Dumbledore's Deluminator is bequeathed to Ron, described as valuable, possibly unique, and of Dumbledore's own design, then shown removing and restoring lamplight.
- `dh-ch07-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Seven - The Will of Albus Dumbledore): Dumbledore leaves Harry the Snitch from his first Hogwarts Quidditch match; Scrimgeour explains Snitch flesh memory, and Harry later reveals a temporary Dumbledore inscription.
- `dh-ch08-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eight - The Wedding): Krum confirms Gregorovitch as a celebrated retired wandmaker and frames a non-British reputation for wand quality alongside British reliance on Ollivander.
- `dh-ch08-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eight - The Wedding): The scene contrasts Doge's admiring obituary with Skeeter's hostile biography and records both as competing public sources about Dumbledore's past.
- `dh-ch08-007` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eight - The Wedding): Kingsley uses a speaking corporeal Patronus to announce the Ministry's fall, Scrimgeour's death, and the imminent arrival of hostile forces.
- `dh-ch09-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Nine - A Place to Hide): The Ministry takeover is followed immediately by the collapse of the Burrow's wedding protections, Death Eaters appearing among guests, and Order members casting Protego while the trio escapes.
- `dh-ch09-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Nine - A Place to Hide): Hermione's beaded bag holds emergency clothing, the Invisibility Cloak, Harry's rucksack, and books by means of an Undetectable Extension Charm prepared before the attack.
- `dh-ch09-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Nine - A Place to Hide): Hermione treats Muggle London as an unexpected refuge, yet Death Eaters still locate the trio in a cafe, causing wand combat and a Muggle witness casualty.
- `dh-ch09-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Nine - A Place to Hide): The trio use Memory Charms, restore the damaged cafe, and reverse binding/stunning effects to hide both their presence and visible magical violence from Muggle and Death Eater witnesses.
- `dh-ch09-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Nine - A Place to Hide): Ron states that Wizarding law breaks the Trace at seventeen and bars placing it on an adult, while Hermione raises the wartime fear that Death Eaters might have found a way around that rule.
- `dh-ch09-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Nine - A Place to Hide): Grimmauld Place is visible because Dumbledore had told them the secret; wand entry, gas lamps, Mrs. Black's portrait, Moody's Tongue-Tying Curse and Dumbledore-like dust figure, and Homenum revelio show layered headquarters protections.
- `dh-ch09-007` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Nine - A Place to Hide): Arthur's speaking Patronus confirms the family's survival but warns the trio not to answer because the senders are being watched.
- `dh-ch11-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eleven - The Bribe): After the Ministry falls, Death Eaters use state power to raid the Burrow and Order-connected homes, overcoming protective spells that had previously kept attackers outside.
- `dh-ch11-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eleven - The Bribe): The chapter documents Voldemort's concealed Ministry takeover: Scrimgeour's murder is officially disguised, Thicknesse handles routine governance under Imperius, and the Prophet turns Harry into a public suspect.
- `dh-ch11-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eleven - The Bribe): The new Ministry creates a Muggle-born Register and Registration Commission, alleging that Muggle-born witches and wizards stole magic unless they can prove close wizarding ancestry.
- `dh-ch11-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eleven - The Bribe): Voldemort's regime makes Hogwarts attendance compulsory for young British witches and wizards while requiring official Blood Status proof before students are allowed to attend.
- `dh-ch11-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eleven - The Bribe): Lupin distinguishes the relative protection he experienced at Hogwarts and in the Order from wider wizarding prejudice against werewolves and their families.
- `dh-ch11-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eleven - The Bribe): A Daily Prophet extract from Rita Skeeter's Dumbledore biography uses Bathilda Bagshot's local testimony to advance a contested claim about Ariana's hidden childhood and nonattendance at school.
- `dh-ch11-007` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Eleven - The Bribe): Mundungus's testimony traces Slytherin's locket from Grimmauld Place theft to a Ministry official who used trading-license enforcement as leverage to seize it.
- `dh-ch12-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Twelve - Magic Is Might): The new Ministry-backed school order installs Snape as Hogwarts headmaster and gives the Carrows Muggle Studies and Defense Against the Dark Arts, while Harry infers loyal teachers may remain to protect students.
- `dh-ch12-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Twelve - Magic Is Might): The captured Ministry blocks ordinary Apparition, restricts home Floo connections to senior officials, and relies on employee tokens plus enchanted toilet-cubicle transport for worker entry.
- `dh-ch12-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Twelve - Magic Is Might): The Muggle-born Registration regime is in active operation: missed interrogations are listed publicly, and Yaxley uses a worker's wife's Blood Status case as workplace coercion.
- `dh-ch12-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Twelve - Magic Is Might): Harry's scar vision confirms Voldemort is seeking Gregorovitch, and Harry links that search to Ollivander's inability to explain the wand behavior during the Seven Potters chase.
- `dh-ch12-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Twelve - Magic Is Might): The captured Ministry replaces the golden Atrium fountain with a black-stone Magic Is Might monument depicting Muggles crushed beneath enthroned witches and wizards.
- `dh-ch12-007` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Twelve - Magic Is Might): The Ministry lift announcements map relevant offices: Level Four handles creature regulation and Goblin Liaison, Level Two contains Magical Law Enforcement, Improper Use, Aurors, and Wizengamot administration, and Level One houses the Minister.
- `dh-ch13-001` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Thirteen - The Muggle-born Registration Commission): The Commission operates as a scheduled bureaucratic process with record-keeping, courtrooms, guards, and a daily list of people to be interrogated.
- `dh-ch13-002` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Thirteen - The Muggle-born Registration Commission): The captured Ministry mass-produces anonymous pamphlets that frame Muggle-born people as a danger to a peaceful pure-blood society.
- `dh-ch13-003` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Thirteen - The Muggle-born Registration Commission): Umbridge has repurposed Alastor Moody's magical eye as a peephole and telescopic surveillance device in her Ministry office door.
- `dh-ch13-004` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Thirteen - The Muggle-born Registration Commission): The Ministry keeps blood-status and security files on Arthur Weasley, tying family details and Hogwarts-attending children to surveillance of Harry's possible contacts.
- `dh-ch13-005` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Thirteen - The Muggle-born Registration Commission): Blood-status enforcement includes informants and family-tree investigations, with alleged false ancestry records exposing people such as Dirk Cresswell to Azkaban.
- `dh-ch13-006` (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Chapter Thirteen - The Muggle-born Registration Commission): The Commission hearing uses dementors, a chained chair, and prosecutor-side Patronus protection so despair falls on accused Muggle-borns rather than officials.

- `gof-ch28-005` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Twenty-Eight - The Madness of Mr. Crouch): Crouch's appearance on the forest edge combines tournament-administration fragments with an urgent security warning linking Bertha Jorkins, his son, Harry, and Voldemort's growing strength.

- `gof-ch34-004` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Four - Priori Incantatem): The chapter records Priori Incantatem producing wand echoes of Voldemort's recent victims, creating magical evidence for Cedric's murder, Bertha Jorkins's death, and the Potter murders.

- `gof-ch35-002` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Five - Veritaserum): The chapter names the apparent Hogwarts teacher as the internal agent who bypassed the Goblet's entry assumptions by submitting Harry under a different school.

- `gof-ch35-004` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Five - Veritaserum): The chapter confirms that the final-task maze was actively sabotaged from the patrol perimeter, including attacks on champions and manipulation of obstacles.

- `gof-ch35-006` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Five - Veritaserum): The chapter reveals that a complex magical trunk in a Hogwarts office concealed the real Moody all year while the impostor maintained his disguise with hourly Polyjuice Potion.
- `gof-ch35-007` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Five - Veritaserum): The chapter records a staff-led emergency interrogation using Veritaserum obtained from the Potions master, turning classroom-threat potion lore into formal crisis evidence.
- `gof-ch36-001` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Parting of the Ways): The chapter records the staff chain of command after the impostor is exposed, combining prisoner custody, medical transfer for the real Moody, and Ministerial notification.
- `gof-ch36-002` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Parting of the Ways): The chapter shows a Head of House acting as the appropriate staff member to accompany and support a dead student's parents after a school tragedy.
- `gof-ch36-003` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Parting of the Ways): The chapter shows Dumbledore taking an immediate survivor account in the headmaster's office while balancing witness evidence, emotional harm, and magical comfort from Fawkes.
- `gof-ch36-004` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Parting of the Ways): The chapter records a Ministry security breach inside Hogwarts when Fudge brings in a Dementor that destroys Crouch's capacity to testify.
- `gof-ch36-005` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Parting of the Ways): The chapter gives Fudge's explicit account of Dumbledore's broad practical autonomy over Hogwarts staffing and curriculum, followed by a threat of Ministry scrutiny.
- `gof-ch36-006` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Six - The Parting of the Ways): The chapter shows Hogwarts becoming the staging point for Dumbledore's first organized response to Voldemort's return, including Ministry contacts, giant envoys, house-elf care, old allies, and Snape's mission.

- `gof-ch37-002` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Beginning): Dumbledore addresses the school after the maze crisis to limit student questioning of Harry, and the exposed impostor's removal leaves Defense Against the Dark Arts lessons temporarily vacant.

- `gof-ch37-006` (Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Chapter Thirty-Seven - The Beginning): The chapter reveals that Skeeter's Hogwarts reporting depended on illegal Animagus surveillance across school spaces, including the hospital wing and classrooms.

- `hbp-ch01-001` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter One - The Other Minister): The chapter establishes a standing secret contact protocol between the Minister of Magic and the Muggle Prime Minister, using an office portrait and Floo arrival while limiting disclosure to the current Muggle head of government.
- `hbp-ch01-002` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter One - The Other Minister): Fudge defines the Ministry's remit as governing the hidden wizarding community and preserving secrecy, with examples ranging from responsible broomstick use to dragon-population control.
- `hbp-ch01-003` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter One - The Other Minister): Fudge's prior briefings show that the Minister informs the Muggle Prime Minister about magical events that may affect Muggles, including Azkaban escapes, World Cup memory work, and importation of dragons and a sphinx for the Triwizard Tournament.
- `hbp-ch01-004` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter One - The Other Minister): The chapter reframes Muggle public disasters as Second War attacks, naming Voldemort's blackmail over the Brockdale Bridge, Ministry-wide Auror pursuit, suspected giant involvement, the Office of Misinformation, Obliviators, and Magical Creatures staff in Somerset.
- `hbp-ch01-005` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter One - The Other Minister): Fudge reports that Amelia Bones, head of Magical Law Enforcement, was likely murdered by Voldemort personally after putting up a strong fight, while Muggle authorities see only a baffling locked-room killing.
- `hbp-ch01-006` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter One - The Other Minister): Fudge confirms that the dementors no longer guard Azkaban, have joined Voldemort, are breeding, and are causing the unnatural mist and widespread despair in Muggle Britain.
- `hbp-ch01-007` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter One - The Other Minister): The chapter dates Fudge's dismissal and Scrimgeour's accession, shows Kingsley Shacklebolt embedded as an Auror protecting the Muggle Prime Minister, and records St. Mungo's Healers handling an Imperius-damaged Junior Minister.

- `hbp-ch02-004` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Two - Spinner's End): Snape says the Fidelius-style protection around Order headquarters prevents him from speaking the place's name because he is not the Secret-Keeper, though he can pass other operational information.
- `hbp-ch02-005` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Two - Spinner's End): Snape recalls that when Harry first arrived at Hogwarts, rumors circulated among Voldemort's followers that Harry might be a powerful Dark wizard, and Snape later claims he tried to have Harry expelled rather than risk killing him near Dumbledore.
- `hbp-ch02-006` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Two - Spinner's End): The scene demonstrates the Unbreakable Vow procedure: the parties clasp right hands, a Bonder touches them with a wand, and each sworn promise produces binding tongues of flame.
- `hbp-ch03-001` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Three - Will and Won't): A Daily Prophet report brings the secret Department of Mysteries conflict into public circulation, framing Harry as the possible subject of a prophecy and naming Death Eaters sentenced for trespass and attempted theft.
- `hbp-ch03-002` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Three - Will and Won't): Scrimgeour's Ministry publicly claims new wartime Hogwarts protections, including defensive spells, countercurses, and a small Auror task force assigned only to the school.
- `hbp-ch03-003` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Three - Will and Won't): A Ministry household-security leaflet recommends emergency measures against Death Eaters, including Shield and Disillusionment Charms, Side-Along Apparition for underage family members, identity questions, and reporting Imperius, Dark Mark, or Inferius signs.
- `hbp-ch03-004` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Three - Will and Won't): Dumbledore says Black family inheritance traditions or enchantments may force Grimmauld Place down the pure-blood Black line, and that the Order cannot assume its Unplottable protections still hold after ownership transfers.
- `hbp-ch03-005` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Three - Will and Won't): Kreacher's forced obedience confirms Harry's ownership of him, and Dumbledore suggests sending him to Hogwarts kitchens so the other house-elves can supervise a politically dangerous servant.
- `hbp-ch03-006` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Three - Will and Won't): Buckbeak passes to Harry with Sirius's estate, remains in Hagrid's care, and receives the temporary alias Witherwings to protect him from Ministry recognition after the earlier execution sentence.

- `hbp-ch29-005` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Twenty-Nine - The Phoenix Lament): After Dumbledore's death, McGonagall inherits the headmaster's office as headmistress, and Dumbledore immediately appears among the portraits of dead Hogwarts heads.

- `hbp-ch30-004` (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, Chapter Thirty - The White Tomb): Magical residents and non-human communities around Hogwarts join Dumbledore's funeral: merpeople sing in the lake, Grawp mourns beside Hagrid, and centaurs observe from the Forest before offering arrows as tribute.
